summary: The change in public/auth.js makes the email field read-only and hidden only when the authenticated account already has an email, allowing accounts without an email to enter one during backup-password setup. Existing-email accounts remain locked, and the skip path is unchanged.

evidence: public/auth.js:391 now sets emailInput.readOnly to Boolean(emailInput.value), so an empty email leaves the field editable while an existing email stays read-only.
public/auth.js:392 reveals the #email-field label when the value is empty, so the user can see and fill the email input.

public/auth.js:499 validates the entered email before continueWithPassword submits it to /api/auth/password/register, whose server handler attaches the email and password for a hub user without an email (src/passport.ts:653-669).
public/auth.js:397 keeps skipPasswordField visible, retaining the skip option.
